analysis.title: The State of AI Financing: Hyperscalers Are Back
key_insights: Hyperscalers priced about $67bn of unsecured IG bonds (US and EUR) between Oct 29 and Nov 4, showing credit markets remain open. MS expects little or no further unsecured hyperscaler issuance through year-end because of elevated cash balances and alternative funding such as chip financing.

AI and data center debt supply is $646bn YTD, about 3x FY25 ($216bn). Hyperscaler total issuance is $321bn YTD vs $93bn YTD-25. About $210bn of hyperscaler equity issuance was also announced YTD, with some ATM programs not yet completed.

Midterms shift timing but not aggregate capex. MS equity colleagues keep 2027 capex at about $1.66tr (+75% vs 2026) and 2028 at about $1.77tr. About 5 GW of US IT capacity moves from 2028 to 2029, mainly Texas and Ohio projects not yet under construction, and 2027 capacity is unchanged.

MS's Powering AI model now projects a 44 GW net US power shortfall through 2028, up from 38 GW, equal to 38% of modeled data-center power demand. This raises the scarcity value of existing power-secured capacity.

MS sees a widening quality divide in AI credit. Risk-reward for high-quality (HQ) hyperscalers (AMZN, GOOGL, META, MSFT) is improving, and they trade at levels consistent with A/BBB ratings, near YTD wides. Data center construction bonds and neoclouds face more spread volatility from construction and funding risk.

AI-related leveraged finance supply was only $5bn in October (the Volta term loan). MS expects limited supply through year-end because of higher Treasury yields, policy changes, and concerns about neocloud access to credit.

Data center ABS spreads widened sharply in October, with another $2bn pricing across three deals. Prints included the widest AAA ever (200bp), the widest A/A- since mid-2023 (325bp), and the widest BBB/BBB- since fall 2023 (375bp on a 1.5y bond). MS attributes this to structure and supply technicals rather than a change in view on AI.

MS expects ABS demand to recover only if structures partly or fully delever. Investors want amortization. Obstacles include leases struck in a different rate environment, DSCR cash-sweep triggers starting around 1.35, about $45bn of outstanding paper that could be orphaned in old trusts, and short-term colocation leases.

Chip financing is accelerating, with $103bn announced in October and $138bn YTD. MS expects SPV chip financing to be a meaningful part of AI supply over the next twelve months. These deals are shorter, within 5 years, so MS expects further curve flattening.

The HQ hyperscaler cohort trades 9bp wider than the IG index. YTD spread widening is 116bp for LQ hyperscalers (ORCL, SPCX), 54bp for NVDA+AVGO, 40bp for HQ hypers, and 13bp for the IG index. The AI CDS basket trades about 85bp wider than CDX IG, and MSFT 5Y CDS is the only HQ name still tighter than CDX IG.

Recent deals have mostly tightened since issuance (MSFT, META, GOOGL EUR), but ORCL is the exception. ORCL's 2031 and 2037 tranches are 12bp and 9bp wider since issue on the $10bn deal. META's EUR deal drew a record EUR62.1bn order book (6.9x) on EUR9bn.

ORCL Analyst Day: about $20bn of remaining FY27 funding needs, split evenly between debt and equity, with no further external capital expected thereafter excluding refinancing. Management implied tens of billions of 5Y vendor financing and customer prepayments to support more than $200bn medium-term capex. MS removed the 30Y from its recommended trade expression. A $10bn bond and $10bn equity raise followed.

Off-balance-sheet leverage is rising. Hyperscalers disclose $1.3tr of leases not yet commenced and about $2.18tr of purchase commitments. MS forecasts $195bn of leased data center shells in 2027. Hyperscalers, NVDA and AVGO disclose about $4tr of off-balance-sheet commitments and guarantees.

Neocloud stress is visible. CRWV unsecured debt reached CCC-like spreads in October (about 1,156bp on the 2030s). CRWV equity is down 49.4% over a month and 35.2% YTD. HY data center bonds are about 275bp wide to the BB index.

Upcoming off-cycle semiconductor and hardware earnings, including NVDA and DELL, are a focus for bespoke chip and supplier financing. DELL's DFS-related debt exceeded $20bn last quarter, vs about $14bn implied by core debt, and MS sees near-term DELL spread pressure as warranted pending clarity on its finco role. AMZN disclosed a secured supplier-financing facility of up to $80bn.

market_movers.rationale: MS credit keeps a Buy 5Y CDS trade (entry +57bp, now +307bp) and a Sell on the ORCL 5.2% 9/26/35 bond (entry +167bp, now +300bp). It cites cash funding needs, lease liabilities and vendor financing that could prime unsecured creditors.
MS sees near-term spread pressure as warranted pending clarity on the finco's role in AI server financing. Receivables rose last quarter and the company reports again later this month.
Unsecured bonds trade at CCC-type spreads and the stock is down sharply. Higher funding costs and heavy reliance on external capital are the stated risks for neoclouds.
Further chip financing disclosures in its upcoming FY3Q27 print are highly anticipated by credit investors.
MSFT's October-November bonds have tightened since issue, and its 5Y CDS is the only HQ hyperscaler still trading tighter than CDX IG.

sector_views.rationale: Risk-reward is improving. They are well capitalized, trade at A/BBB-consistent levels near YTD wides, and have 1.2x gross leverage and 118% cash-to-debt.

sector_views.sector: Data center construction bonds and neoclouds
sector_views.rationale: More spread volatility is expected from construction risk, funding risk and political scrutiny of permitting and power access.
Spreads are at the year's wides on structure and supply technicals. Demand needs amortizing structures or deleveraging to return.
Supply should stay subdued with a higher bar for new deals. Expect new deals to need greater construction-risk premiums, lower loan-to-cost and more amortization.

tension_points.bull_case: HQ hyperscalers have 1.2x gross leverage, 118% cash-to-debt, and record demand (META EUR book 6.9x). MS says risk-reward is as good as it has been all year, with spreads near YTD wides at A/BBB-consistent levels.
tension_points.bear_case: Off-balance-sheet leases ($1.3tr not yet started) and purchase commitments (about $2.18tr) are rising. Peak negative FCF is expected next year. Supplier financing could prime unsecured creditors, and HQ hyperscaler spreads have widened YTD (HQ hypers +40bp).
tension_points.what_invalidates: A cut to aggregate capex forecasts, or more equity and funding transactions needed to close the gap between investment and monetization.

tension_points.bull_case: MS sees the weakness as technical, not a view on AI. Completion premiums offer a buffer, so issuers can keep widening spreads to get deals done. Amortizing structures could bring meaningful spread tightening from AAA at 200bp.
tension_points.bear_case: The market is approaching saturation for this structure. Order books are harder to fill, single-A spreads are above 300bp, and amortization faces DSCR trigger, legacy lease and orphaned-trust obstacles.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Continued difficulty filling order books at wider spreads would force issuers to restructure their financing, per MS's second phase.
